name: service-bus
description: Enterprise message broker for async communication, queues, and pub/sub topics

defaultConfig.note: Basic for simple queues (~$0.05/million ops). Standard for topics/subscriptions (~$10/month). Premium for VNet + large messages (~$668/month).

integration.authNote: Use DefaultAzureCredential with Service Bus Data Sender/Receiver roles. No connection strings needed. Namespace FQDN is used as the endpoint.

appSettings.name: AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_QUEUE_NAME
appSettings.description: Queue name (or topic name for pub/sub)

sdkInitPattern.python:
from azure.servicebus.aio import ServiceBusClient
from azure.identity.aio import DefaultAzureCredential

credential = DefaultAzureCredential(managed_identity_client_id=os.environ.get('AZURE_CLIENT_ID'))
client = ServiceBusClient(
    fully_qualified_namespace=os.environ['AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_NAMESPACE'],
    credential=credential
)

# Send message
async with client.get_queue_sender(os.environ['AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_QUEUE_NAME']) as sender:
    await sender.send_messages(ServiceBusMessage(body))

# Receive messages
async with client.get_queue_receiver(os.environ['AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_QUEUE_NAME']) as receiver:
    messages = await receiver.receive_messages(max_message_count=10)
    for msg in messages:
        await receiver.complete_message(msg)

healthCheck.python:
# Peek a message (non-destructive) to validate connectivity
async with client.get_queue_receiver(queue_name) as receiver:
    await receiver.peek_messages(max_message_count=1)
healthCheck.description: Peek validates connectivity and permissions without consuming messages
